evidence.notes: Scope honoured: this groom writes ONLY the card, its byte-identical mirror, and this handoff. No generator, test, report, index or application file is touched (ac7 proves the delta is documentation-only). scratch/ holds throwaway build and validation helpers and is NOT committed - which is why every rc, evidence line and negative-control observation is transcribed into this handoff rather than left in a directory that vanishes with the worktree. FILENAME DEVIATION, recorded deliberately: the dispatch named docs/state/outputs/t59_groom.json, and that path is used here even though t57/t58 used t5X_definer_groom.json; the dispatch is authoritative over precedent, and the ac7 authorisation whitelist 'docs/state/outputs/t59_[a-z_]+.json' admits both spellings so the builder may add t59_builder_implement.json etc. without a card edit. Three things a reviewer should check rather than trust: (1) the ac_hash recipe was validated against a MERGED precedent before being trusted here - recomputing it over docs/issues/closed/t58.md reproduces that card's own pin exactly; (2) the pin changed mid-groom (142f8a36 -> 58f2a24c) when the inner-syntax check exposed the stray ';;' in ac6, so any reference to the older value is stale; (3) six fences are green at base, which is what an exit composite looks like, and each carries a control that can fail it. Residual risks disclosed: the attestation is time-bound to one commit, and the frontend legs of ac1/ac3/ac5 are prerequisite-gated, so a run without frontend/node_modules attests strictly less - the fences print an explicit prerequisite line instead of passing silently, and the reader should read the evidence line, not only the exit code.
